messages:
marta: Heads-up — customer reported missing KMS audit entries after we tightened RBAC on their private deploy. They see successful responses from keystore but nothing in the central KMS audit stream :thinking:
liam: Which keystore path? proxy -> external KMS or our local HSM shim?
jordan: root: it’s the onprem keystore-proxy talking to customer HSM via internal TLS. They trimmed some sa roles yesterday (k8s).
marta: Right. We removed the broad 'keystore:admin' blanket and split into two fine-grained roles; one of the service accounts lost kms:decrypt on the HSM-side wrapper.
natalie: If the service account lost decrypt, why are responses still successful? should be 403 right?
marta: That's the weird part — the keystore-proxy has a local cache fallback. If HSM call fails it serves cached CEK and doesn't emit the external KMS audit event (we only log HSM success/fail, not cache-sourced decrypts).
liam: Ah — so RBAC change triggered HSM deny, then proxy silently served cached keys => no remote audit entries. Bad visible signal.
jordan: We need two fixes: 1) ensure keystore-proxy logs fallback events to audit stream; 2) ensure RBAC denies are obvious and block fallback for high-sensitivity tenants.
marta: Agreed. Short-term: disable cache fallback for that tenant and rotate any keys used. Also notify customer.
sre-oncall: I can roll a hotfix to flip off fallback flag in the private deploys config. ETA ~10m.
audit-bot: NOTE: Missing external KMS audit events marked as severity:medium for tenant t-42. Ticket #SEC-1098 created.
natalie: For network part — their netpol tightening earlier allowed hostNetwork pods for monitoring; that may be what let the proxy reach local cache path? Not sure.
liam: HostNetwork shouldn't affect local cache. But hostNetwork can bypass namespace netpols and accidentally expose admin endpoints across tenant nodes. We should check if the keystore admin socket was reachable from other namespaces.
marta: Action items: liam verify netpols + hostNetwork exposure, natalie push fallback=false for tenant t-42, jordan add audit log for fallback events, and rotate keys. I'll draft customer note.
liam: Checking now — running conntrack and iptables snapshot on node-7: `sudo conntrack -L | grep keystore` and `ss -xlpn | grep keystore`
jordan: For the long term: (a) add an explicit audit flag when proxy serves cached CEK: `audit.event = keystore.fallback_cache_serve`, (b) require HSM success for tenants with compliance tag `pci/sox` unless explicit allowlist, (c) netpol linter to flag hostNetwork usage in private deployments.
marta: Also add a prom counter `keystore_cache_fallback_total{tenant}` so SLO can alert.
audit-bot: SEC-1098 updated: remediation steps added and stakeholders pinged.
sre-oncall: Hotfix applied — fallback disabled for t-42, keystore proxy restarted. Observability: I see 3 fallback events in the last 12h prior to restart.
marta: Good. Next: rotate CEKs and coordinate with customer for re-encrypting stored tokens.
liam: Netpol finding: one monitoring pod had hostNetwork=true and clusterRole binding allowed access to keystore admin port 9211 on node IPs. Suggest we deny hostNetwork for non-system namespaces and add admission hook.
natalie: I can prototype an admission webhook to deny hostNetwork + require annotation `privileged-network: true` for allowed exceptions.
jordan: Leave a follow-up ticket to add audit events to central log pipeline and create an eval that simulates RBAC deny -> fallback to catch regressions.
marta: I'll send the customer a short incident note saying we disabled fallback, rotating keys, and we will follow up with a permanent fix next week. :thumbsup:
